findings.title: File-level selector is an exclusion, not the architecture's allow-list, and the drift guard can't catch the failure it creates
findings.description:
The architecture defines file-level types as a closed set of nine and says function- and class-level nodes "are not read" (`360-arch` §Read discipline). Line 151 says the selector "becomes an explicit type allow-list". Lines 155-158 then specify `select(.type != "function" and .type != "class")` and argue against an allow-list. The document contradicts itself, and the design it settles on departs from the architecture.

The rationale is that a new file-level type gets included automatically. The same goes for any new **sub-file** type a later upstream release adds (e.g. `method`, `interface`, `variable`). Those would also be included automatically, which breaks the read discipline that exists because of graph size. The guard ("surviving node with no `filePath` is drift") doesn't help: sub-file nodes carry a path too (their ids are `function:path:name`). So the failure would be silent, which goes against the architecture's rule that upstream drift must "surface as a loud failure".

Fix: use the architecture's nine-type allow-list. Report any node type outside both the allow-list and `{function, class}` as upstream drift. New types then show up loudly in either direction.

findings.title: Dependency observations need function/class node data, against the architecture and SC 9
findings.description:
Line 218-220 says function- and class-level edge endpoints "are resolved to their owning file's layer rather than dropped". That means mapping `function:*`/`class:*` ids to files. The design doesn't say how: parsing the id prefix (which is ambiguous if paths contain `:`), walking `contains` edges, or reading the sub-file nodes' `filePath`. The last option breaks the architecture's "function- and class-level nodes are not read" rule and the slice's own Success Criterion 9 ("no function- or class-level node is read", line 333).

The section also contradicts itself on scope. Line 215 limits inter-layer counting to `imports` and `depends_on`, but line 219 counts `calls` edges too. The tie-break "by `weight`" (mapping row 6) is undefined for aggregated counts (sum? max?). `edges[].direction` is listed as an input (line 85) and never used.

Fix: either drop sub-file endpoints, which matches 361's original edge-aggregate scope, or name a resolution method that reads only edge ids. Then pick one edge-type set and define how weight is aggregated.

findings.title: Coverage reconciliation and "file-level = has `filePath`" are generalized from a graph with 3 of 9 file-level types
findings.description:
The measured graph has only `file`, `config` and `pipeline` among file-level types (line 98). The architecture's set also includes `service`, `endpoint`, `schema`, `table`, `document` and `resource`. Several of those can be many-per-file (several `endpoint`s or `schema`s in one source file). In a graph that has them, "file-level node count == `analyzedFiles`" won't hold, and neither will "every file in exactly one layer" as the design reads it.

Lines 224-227 then tell the skill to report a mismatch as "the graph is internally inconsistent". That's a confident wrong claim in exactly the case the design never measured. The Risk Assessment (lines 439-445) admits single-graph risk for Correction 1 but not for the coverage reconciliation.

Fix: describe a mismatch neutrally, reporting both numbers without asserting inconsistency. Add the reconciliation to the single-graph risk paragraph.

findings.title: The `[INFERRED]` exception's own example fails its test and invites copying
findings.description:
Closing observations are allowed if they're "derivable from the table directly above". The example given, "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK", can't be derived from a tier/layer table. "Seams" and "external SDK" are interpretation, which is what the architecture's "never fabricate" goal and this section's "zero `[INFERRED]`" decision forbid. A concrete example sentence carried into the skill text is also a template the generating model is likely to copy.

Fix: give a derivable example ("N of M `complex` nodes are in layer X"), or require that the observation cite the counts it summarizes.

findings.title: Small internal inconsistencies
findings.description:
- Lines 234-235 say an all-comments `.understandignore` is "defaults only", but the parenthetical says this repo has 17 active lines. The two don't match. Mapping row 7 also treats an unreadable/absent `.understandignore` as a gap, but the file is optional upstream, so absence should probably read as "defaults only" too.
- Line 42 says everything is "within `understand.md`", while lines 279 and 336-338 also edit `user/reference/analyze-codebase-prompt.md`. SC 11 calls that a "non-document file", but it's a document.
- The ordering rule "layer, then `filePath`" for entry points doesn't say which layer order to use (presumably the same descending file count as section 2).

findings.title: Mapping is overclaimed as "reused verbatim" by 363
findings.description: The architecture already defines 363's per-concept-section field mapping (`360-arch` §Interview scope). 362's table maps fields to *comprehension* sections. What 363 actually reuses is the field selectors and the corrected file-level definition, not the section mapping itself. The Integration Points wording at lines 299-301 is accurate. The Value paragraph overstates it.

findings.title: Correction claims rely on 361 artifacts that aren't in this tree
findings.description:
Neither `commands/analysis/understand.md` nor the `943` sample exists in this checkout (`analysis/` holds 940-942 only). So I couldn't check the "361 skill text" defects against the source. Walkthrough step 1 re-measures before implementation and stops on disagreement, which is the right mitigation.

The walkthrough's `git diff --stat main -- src/` (line 429) hardcodes `main`. It should diff against the configured integration target.
